The ouruin_level hotspot script listens to level messages called from aschar.as and increments lethality counts respectively.
When the game needs to load a new level, the lethality_tally level message is received, and then waits for the tally to finish.

Each elimination, kill, overkill, alert, throat cut and zone kill is added up, and then converted into (multiplied) points.
These points are added up into a total, and that total is compared to a ratio (defined in Data/Dialogues/ouruin/enemy_ids.txt).
Based on this ratio, the level is assigned a lethality value from 0 to 6.

Lastly, every level's lethality value is added together, and then averaged based on which levels have so far been visited.
This is the campaign's total average lethality, and is used for lethality checks in dialogue or otherwise.

Once all of this is finished, the tally hotspot finally returns a level message to continue loading the new level.


NOTE: Each level must pass their current and stored alerts to a specific faction's!

eliminations
 Add 1 lethality point
kills
 Add 8 lethality points
zonekills
 Add 2 lethality points. Incurred upon drowning, dying to spikes, or lava
overkills
 Add 2 lethality points per overkill. Maximum of 10 overkills per level for a total of 20 points
throatscut
 Add 4 lethality points
 


At the end of every level, Ouruin adds up each elimination, kill and overkill.
These variables are then tallied to form a total number of points.
This point total is compared to a percentage of the maximum possible lethality points (not counting throats slit and overkills).

--!! CONSULT Data/Dialogues/ouruin/enemy_ids.txt !!--

(0) Perfect Non-Lethal Stealth requires 0% lethality points.
(1) Non-Lethal Stealth requires less than 10% lethality points.
(2) Non-Lethal requires less than 25% lethality points.
(3) Lethal requires less than 50% lethality points.
(4) Full-Lethal requires more than 75% lethality points.
(5) Perfect Full-Lethal requires 100% lethality points.
(6) Senseless Full-Lethal requires more than 100% lethality points.

{"functions":[{"display_comment":"~!!! documentation !!!~

The ouruin_level hotspot script listens to level messages called from aschar.as and increments lethality counts respectively.
When the game needs to load a new level, the lethality_tally level message is received, and then waits for the tally to finish.

Each elimination, kill, overkill, alert, throat cut and zone kill is added up, and then converted into (multiplied) points.
These points are added up into a total, and that total is compared to a ratio (defined in Data/Dialogues/ouruin/enemy_ids.txt).
Based on this ratio, the level is assigned a lethality value from 0 to 6.

Lastly, every level's lethality value is added together, and then averaged based on which levels have so far been visited.
This is the campaign's total average lethality, and is used for lethality checks in dialogue or otherwise.

Once all of this is finished, the tally hotspot finally returns a level message to continue loading the new level.


NOTE: Each level must pass their current and stored alerts to a specific faction's!

{"functions":[{"display_comment":"~!!! documentation !!!~

The ouruin_level hotspot script listens to level messages called from aschar.as and increments lethality counts respectively.
When the game needs to load a new level, the lethality_tally level message is received, and then waits for the tally to finish.

Each elimination, kill, overkill, alert, throat cut and zone kill is added up, and then converted into (multiplied) points.
These points are added up into a total, and that total is compared to a ratio (defined in Data/Dialogues/ouruin/enemy_ids.txt).
Based on this ratio, the level is assigned a lethality value from 0 to 6.

Lastly, every level's lethality value is added together, and then averaged based on which levels have so far been visited.
This is the campaign's total average lethality, and is used for lethality checks in dialogue or otherwise.

Once all of this is finished, the tally hotspot finally returns a level message to continue loading the new level.


NOTE: Each level must pass their current and stored alerts to a specific faction's!

eliminations

kills

zonekills

overkills
 Add 2 lethality points per overkill. Maximum of 10 overkills per level for a total of 20 points

At the end of every level, Ouruin adds up each elimination, kill and overkill.
These variables are then tallied to form a total number of points.
This point total is compared to a percentage of the maximum possible lethality points (not counting throats slit and overkills).

(0) Perfect Non-Lethal Stealth requires 0% lethality points.
(1) Non-Lethal Stealth requires less than 10% lethality points.
(2) Non-Lethal requires less than 25% lethality points.
(3) Lethal requires less than 50% lethality points.
(4) Full-Lethal requires more than 75% lethality points.
(5) Perfect Full-Lethal requires 100% lethality points.
(6) Senseless Full-Lethal requires more than 100% lethality points.

{"functions":[{"display_comment":"~!!! documentation !!!~

The ouruin_level hotspot script listens to level messages called from aschar.as and increments lethality counts respectively.
When the game needs to load a new level, the lethality_tally level message is received, and then waits for the tally to finish.

Each elimination, kill, overkill, alert, throat cut and zone kill is added up, and then converted into (multiplied) points.
These points are added up into a total, and that total is compared to a ratio (defined in Data/Dialogues/ouruin/enemy_ids.txt).
Based on this ratio, the level is assigned a lethality value from 0 to 6.

Lastly, every level's lethality value is added together, and then averaged based on which levels have so far been visited.
This is the campaign's total average lethality, and is used for lethality checks in dialogue or otherwise.

Once all of this is finished, the tally hotspot finally returns a level message to continue loading the new level.


NOTE: Each level must pass their current and stored alerts to a specific faction's!

At the end of every level, Ouruin adds up each elimination, kill and overkill.
These variables are then tallied to form a total number of points.
This point total is compared to a percentage of the maximum possible lethality points (not counting throats slit and overkills).

--!! CONSULT Data/Dialogues/ouruin/enemy_ids.txt !!--

(0) Perfect Non-Lethal Stealth requires 0% lethality points.
(1) Non-Lethal Stealth requires less than 10% lethality points.
(2) Non-Lethal requires less than 25% lethality points.
(3) Lethal requires less than 50% lethality points.
(4) Full-Lethal requires more than 75% lethality points.
(5) Perfect Full-Lethal requires 100% lethality points.
(6) Senseless Full-Lethal requires more than 100% lethality points.

{"functions":[{"display_comment":"~!!! documentation !!!~

The ouruin_level hotspot script listens to level messages called from aschar.as and increments lethality counts respectively.
When the game needs to load a new level, the lethality_tally level message is received, and then waits for the tally to finish.

Each elimination, kill, overkill, alert, throat cut and zone kill is added up, and then converted into (multiplied) points.
These points are added up into a total, and that total is compared to a ratio (defined in Data/Dialogues/ouruin/enemy_ids.txt).
Based on this ratio, the level is assigned a lethality value from 0 to 6.

Lastly, every level's lethality value is added together, and then averaged based on which levels have so far been visited.
This is the campaign's total average lethality, and is used for lethality checks in dialogue or otherwise.

Once all of this is finished, the tally hotspot finally returns a level message to continue loading the new level.


NOTE: Each level must pass their current and stored alerts to a specific faction's!

eliminations

zonekills

At the end of every level, Ouruin adds up each elimination, kill and overkill.
These variables are then tallied to form a total number of points.
This point total is compared to a percentage of the maximum possible lethality points (not counting throats slit and overkills).

--!! CONSULT Data/Dialogues/ouruin/enemy_ids.txt !!--

(0) Perfect Non-Lethal Stealth requires 0% lethality points.
(1) Non-Lethal Stealth requires less than 10% lethality points.
(2) Non-Lethal requires less than 25% lethality points.
(3) Lethal requires less than 50% lethality points.
(4) Full-Lethal requires more than 75% lethality points.
(5) Perfect Full-Lethal requires 100% lethality points.
(6) Senseless Full-Lethal requires more than 100% lethality points.

{"functions":[{"display_comment":"~!!! documentation !!!~

The ouruin_level hotspot script listens to level messages called from aschar.as and increments lethality counts respectively.
When the game needs to load a new level, the lethality_tally level message is received, and then waits for the tally to finish.

Each elimination, kill, overkill, alert, throat cut and zone kill is added up, and then converted into (multiplied) points.
These points are added up into a total, and that total is compared to a ratio (defined in Data/Dialogues/ouruin/enemy_ids.txt).
Based on this ratio, the level is assigned a lethality value from 0 to 6.

Lastly, every level's lethality value is added together, and then averaged based on which levels have so far been visited.
This is the campaign's total average lethality, and is used for lethality checks in dialogue or otherwise.

Once all of this is finished, the tally hotspot finally returns a level message to continue loading the new level.


NOTE: Each level must pass their current and stored alerts to a specific faction's!

eliminations

kills
 Add 8 lethality points
zonekills
 Add 2 lethality points. Incurred upon drowning, dying to spikes, or lava
overkills
 Add 2 lethality points per overkill. Maximum of 10 overkills per level for a total of 20 points

At the end of every level, Ouruin adds up each elimination, kill and overkill.
These variables are then tallied to form a total number of points.
This point total is compared to a percentage of the maximum possible lethality points (not counting throats slit and overkills).

--!! CONSULT Data/Dialogues/ouruin/enemy_ids.txt !!--

(0) Perfect Non-Lethal Stealth requires 0% lethality points.
(1) Non-Lethal Stealth requires less than 10% lethality points.
(2) Non-Lethal requires less than 25% lethality points.
(3) Lethal requires less than 50% lethality points.
(4) Full-Lethal requires more than 75% lethality points.
(5) Perfect Full-Lethal requires 100% lethality points.
(6) Senseless Full-Lethal requires more than 100% lethality points.

{"functions":[{"display_comment":"~!!! documentation !!!~

The ouruin_level hotspot script listens to level messages called from aschar.as and increments lethality counts respectively.
When the game needs to load a new level, the lethality_tally level message is received, and then waits for the tally to finish.

Each elimination, kill, overkill, alert, throat cut and zone kill is added up, and then converted into (multiplied) points.
These points are added up into a total, and that total is compared to a ratio (defined in Data/Dialogues/ouruin/enemy_ids.txt).
Based on this ratio, the level is assigned a lethality value from 0 to 6.

Lastly, every level's lethality value is added together, and then averaged based on which levels have so far been visited.
This is the campaign's total average lethality, and is used for lethality checks in dialogue or otherwise.

Once all of this is finished, the tally hotspot finally returns a level message to continue loading the new level.


NOTE: Each level must pass their current and stored alerts to a specific faction's!

At the end of every level, Ouruin adds up each elimination, kill and overkill.
These variables are then tallied to form a total number of points.
This point total is compared to a percentage of the maximum possible lethality points (not counting throats slit and overkills).

--!! CONSULT Data/Dialogues/ouruin/enemy_ids.txt !!--

(0) Perfect Non-Lethal Stealth requires 0% lethality points.
(1) Non-Lethal Stealth requires less than 10% lethality points.
(2) Non-Lethal requires less than 25% lethality points.
(3) Lethal requires less than 50% lethality points.
(4) Full-Lethal requires more than 75% lethality points.
(5) Perfect Full-Lethal requires 100% lethality points.
(6) Senseless Full-Lethal requires more than 100% lethality points.

{"functions":[{"display_comment":"~!!! documentation !!!~

The ouruin_level hotspot script listens to level messages called from aschar.as and increments lethality counts respectively.
When the game needs to load a new level, the lethality_tally level message is received, and then waits for the tally to finish.

Each elimination, kill, overkill, alert, throat cut and zone kill is added up, and then converted into (multiplied) points.
These points are added up into a total, and that total is compared to a ratio (defined in Data/Dialogues/ouruin/enemy_ids.txt).
Based on this ratio, the level is assigned a lethality value from 0 to 6.

Lastly, every level's lethality value is added together, and then averaged based on which levels have so far been visited.
This is the campaign's total average lethality, and is used for lethality checks in dialogue or otherwise.

Once all of this is finished, the tally hotspot finally returns a level message to continue loading the new level.


NOTE: Each level must pass their current and stored alerts to a specific faction's!

eliminations

kills

zonekills

At the end of every level, Ouruin adds up each elimination, kill and overkill.
These variables are then tallied to form a total number of points.
This point total is compared to a percentage of the maximum possible lethality points (not counting throats slit and overkills).

--!! CONSULT Data/Dialogues/ouruin/enemy_ids.txt !!--

(0) Perfect Non-Lethal Stealth requires 0% lethality points.
(1) Non-Lethal Stealth requires less than 10% lethality points.
(2) Non-Lethal requires less than 25% lethality points.
(3) Lethal requires less than 50% lethality points.
(4) Full-Lethal requires more than 75% lethality points.
(5) Perfect Full-Lethal requires 100% lethality points.
(6) Senseless Full-Lethal requires more than 100% lethality points.

{"functions":[{"display_comment":"~!!! documentation !!!~

The ouruin_level hotspot script listens to level messages called from aschar.as and increments lethality counts respectively.
When the game needs to load a new level, the lethality_tally level message is received, and then waits for the tally to finish.

Each elimination, kill, overkill, alert, throat cut and zone kill is added up, and then converted into (multiplied) points.
These points are added up into a total, and that total is compared to a ratio (defined in Data/Dialogues/ouruin/enemy_ids.txt).
Based on this ratio, the level is assigned a lethality value from 0 to 6.

Lastly, every level's lethality value is added together, and then averaged based on which levels have so far been visited.
This is the campaign's total average lethality, and is used for lethality checks in dialogue or otherwise.

Once all of this is finished, the tally hotspot finally returns a level message to continue loading the new level.


NOTE: Each level must pass their current and stored alerts to a specific faction's!

eliminations
 Add 1 lethality point
kills

zonekills

overkills
 Add 2 lethality points per overkill. Maximum of 10 overkills per level for a total of 20 points

At the end of every level, Ouruin adds up each elimination, kill and overkill.
These variables are then tallied to form a total number of points.
This point total is compared to a percentage of the maximum possible lethality points (not counting throats slit and overkills).

--!! CONSULT Data/Dialogues/ouruin/enemy_ids.txt !!--

(0) Perfect Non-Lethal Stealth requires 0% lethality points.
(1) Non-Lethal Stealth requires less than 10% lethality points.
(2) Non-Lethal requires less than 25% lethality points.
(3) Lethal requires less than 50% lethality points.
(4) Full-Lethal requires more than 75% lethality points.
(5) Perfect Full-Lethal requires 100% lethality points.
(6) Senseless Full-Lethal requires more than 100% lethality points.
